name: Da Nang food guide
summary: Da Nang cooks the middle of the country: turmeric noodles at lunch, fish-cake soup in the morning, seafood on the beach road after dark, and a river cafe when you want several plates at one table.
body: Eat Da Nang as its own city. Hoi An’s cao lau is a short ride south, and bun bo Hue is a ride north. The bowl that tells you where you are is mi Quang: wide turmeric noodles, a shallow broth, peanuts, herbs, and a rice cracker you break into the bowl.

The shops below are ones people in the city write down for a friend. A market still works when you are already inside it. Hours move, and a branch can shift. Confirm them when you arrive. On the beach road, ask the price of seafood before it is cooked.
specialtiesLead: These are the dishes to know by name. The shops that cook them are in the sections under this list.

sections.heading: Where to eat
paragraphs: Hai Chau, on the river, is the morning and the lunch. The streets and the two halls are in the next section, with the clocks the city pages actually print. Where two pages disagree, both figures are here.
Nguyễn Chí Thanh is the noodle street: bun cha ca, cao lau, and chicken rice within a few blocks. Bạch Đằng is the river path for coffee and a walk, not a ranked cafe list.

Võ Nguyên Giáp is the beach road. Dinner here is seafood along Hoàng Sa, Võ Nguyên Giáp, and Trường Sa. Ask the price before it is cooked. Nguyễn Phan Vinh, on the Son Tra shore, is the other seafood street. An Thuong, in the lanes just inland of My Khe, is where Korean barbecue and Japanese counters cluster. The page names the quarter, and a shop only when a door was already on this guide.

sections.heading: Food streets and markets
paragraphs: These are areas, not a stall list. A gate fee is not published for the streets below. Check on arrival if someone asks for one. Four other street names appear on a 2020 city page with no block and no hour. They are not mapped here.

spots.name: Huynh Thuc Khang
spots.note: The breakfast street. Busy 06:00–08:00 on the 2020 page. The 2019 page prints 06:00–12:00. Walk the counters. Cao lau on the old list is still the Hoi An noodle.

spots.name: Pham Hong Thai
spots.note: The night eating street, under 800 m on the 2019 page. That page prints 17:00–23:00. A later page names the street and does not restate the clock. Come after dark, not for breakfast.

spots.name: Phan Tu
spots.note: An evening snack street a little over 1 km, near the sea. The 2019 page prints 17:00–24:00. That clock is not restated later.

spots.name: Han Market
spots.address: 119 Trần Phú, by the swing bridge
spots.note: The river hall. The 2023 page prints 06:00–19:00. The 2024 page outlines Trần Phú, Bạch Đằng, Hùng Vương, and Nguyễn Thái Học, and does not restate the clock. The 2023 page names Nguyễn Văn Linh as the fourth side. Use the 2024 block and confirm the door.

spots.name: Con Market
spots.address: Hùng Vương and Ông Ích Khiêm
spots.note: The food hall. Indoor counters and an outdoor row. The 2023 page prints 07:00–19:30 and gives 290 Hùng Vương. The 2024 page puts the crossroads at Quang Trung and Ông Ích Khiêm and prints no clock. Aim for that crossing.

spots.name: Helio
spots.address: 01 đường 2/9, corner of Phan Đăng Lưu
spots.note: A night market of food stalls. The 2023 page prints 17:30–22:30 and a show at 20:00. The 2019 page also prints 17:00–22:30 and says entry is free. The operator site did not load. Confirm the night.

spots.name: Son Tra night market
spots.address: East bank of the Dragon Bridge
spots.note: VietnamPlus, 22 Aug 2025, says the market moved on 1 Aug 2025 to the east bank, in An Hai, and that the road in front is closed to vehicles after 17:30. The 2023 tourism page still says Mai Hắc Đế, 18:00–23:00. The new site has no printed closing hour. Confirm which gate is open.

spots.name: An Thuong night market
spots.note: About 40 stalls on the 2023 page, 17:00–23:00, free entry. This is not the bar lanes. Those are the quarter bounded by Võ Nguyên Giáp, Hoàng Kế Viêm, Châu Thị Vĩnh Tế, and Ngô Thì Sĩ.

spots.name: Bac My An market
spots.note: A neighborhood food hall. The 2019 page prints 08:00–19:00. Later pages name the market and do not restate the door or the clock.

spots.name: Tho Quang
spots.note: The wholesale fish landing, not a mì Quảng stop. The ministry reprint says the yard is busy day and night and does not give a visitor hour. Do not come here for a sit-down lunch.

sections.heading: Noodles
paragraphs: Start with the Da Nang bowls, then the two neighbor noodles if you are not riding that day. Lunch is mi Quang. Morning is bun cha ca.

spots.name: Ba Ngan 3
spots.note: The mi Quang bowl people name when they send a friend. Break the cracker into the bowl and toss. Come at lunch.

spots.name: Ong Ta
spots.note: Bun cha ca in the morning. Fish cakes, a light broth, herbs and chili on the side. Go before the beach.

spots.name: Ba Phien
spots.note: The other morning bowl of bun cha ca. Same order: cakes, broth, herbs. If one room is closed, walk to the other.

spots.name: Hue Thu
spots.note: Banh canh cá lóc, snakehead fish in a thick noodle broth. The page has the street and not a house number. Ask for Huế Thu when you are on it.

spots.name: Ba Van
spots.note: Bun mam with boiled pork. The broth is fermented fish, which is the point. Skip it if that smell is not yours. House number: check on arrival.

spots.name: Hoai Pho
spots.note: Cao lau, the chewy Hoi An noodle with little broth. Eat it here when the old town is not today’s ride. Judge the dish in Hoi An if the bowl is why you go.

spots.name: Ba Huong
spots.note: Bun bo Hue, the spicy beef and pork soup. A Da Nang room for the bowl. The city to judge it in is still Hue.

sections.heading: Rice
paragraphs: Chicken rice is a lunch plate, and the two shops cook it in different traditions. Ask which chicken you are getting.

spots.name: Hong Ngoc
spots.note: Com ga in the Hong Kong style: chicken and seasoned rice. Eat it at lunch, with the dip.

spots.name: Tu Tai
spots.note: Com ga in the Hoi An style. Turmeric rice, chicken, and the sharper central-coast dip. A different plate from Hồng Ngọc, on purpose.

sections.heading: Rolls, cakes, and the stadium plate
paragraphs: These are sitting-down lunches. The rice-paper pork is a shared tray. The stadium plate is the one to cross town for.

spots.name: Ba Huong
spots.address: 364 đường 3/2, and a Duy Tân branch near the airport
spots.note: Boiled pork rolled in rice paper, plus steamed scad, cá nục hấp, rolled the same way. This is a different shop from the bun bo room named Bà Hương. Sit down and share the tray.

spots.name: Tran
spots.note: Banh trang cuon thit heo, pork and herbs in rice paper, with the local dip. Ask what is in the bowl if you skip fermented fish.

spots.name: Ba Be
spots.note: Banh beo, nam, and loc: the set of small steamed cakes. Spoon the dip into the cup. Afternoon is the easy hour.

spots.name: Vit lon um bau
spots.address: Ngô Gia Tự, near Chi Lăng stadium
spots.note: The plate to cross town for. Balut stewed with gourd, and mít trộn, a green jackfruit salad, beside it. Go hungry. There is no house number here. Take the busy stall on that street.

spots.name: Goi ca trich
spots.note: Herring salad with herbs. A shared lunch in the city. The north-shore cousin is gỏi cá Nam Ô, only when you are already riding toward Hai Van.

sections.heading: Seafood
paragraphs: Point at what is fresh, ask for it grilled or steamed, and ask the price before it is cooked. If a number is not agreed, it is not a known price. My Khe is dinner. It is the wrong place to judge a noodle shop.

spots.name: Lao Dai
spots.address: Lô 1 Võ Văn Kiệt, and tables near the Dragon Bridge on Võ Nguyên Giáp
spots.note: The seafood room people put first. Use the Võ Văn Kiệt address, and the beach-road tables by the Dragon Bridge if that is the door you were sent to. Order from the tank, after the price.

spots.name: Ong Minh
spots.note: Seafood on the beach road itself. Same rule: see it, price it, then cook it.

spots.name: Nam Danh
spots.note: The Son Tra shore street. Search Nguyễn Phan Vinh and take the busy room. House number: check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: On the river, start on Huỳnh Thúc Kháng and walk the counters. The city portal’s 2020 page says that street is crowded from 06:00 to 08:00. Its 2019 roundup prints 06:00–12:00. Go early. Bun cha ca, at Ông Tạ or Bà Phiến, is the single bowl if you want one shop. A banh mi is the one you eat standing up, on the way to the beach or the Hoi An road. The beach will feed you. It will not teach you the city.

spots.name: Madame Lan
spots.note: The one table for a Da Nang breakfast. Several local plates, decent cooking, and a real chair, with the river across the road. Come here when you want more than one dish without hunting stalls.

sections.heading: Sweets
paragraphs: Afternoon is chè. The two rooms below are old city shops, the kind parents took their children to, and they are still the ones to name.

spots.name: Che Xuan Trang
spots.note: Bean desserts, chè đậu. An old room on Lê Duẩn, open for decades. Order a bowl and sit.

spots.name: Che Lien
spots.note: Durian dessert, chè sầu riêng. Another long-running shop. Take it only if you want durian. The smell is the dessert.

sections.heading: Coffee and drinks
paragraphs: The phin and condensed milk are still the everyday cup. Matcha is now a normal order beside it, on Bạch Đằng and in the beach cafes. There is no single matcha shop to cross town for. Sit where you already are.
Bạch Đằng is the street for a drink with the river. The beach road is the street for a drink with the sea.

spots.name: Cong
spots.note: The military-green coffee chain, on the river. Iced coffee with condensed milk is the order. You are paying for the chair and the view as much as the cup.

spots.name: Dua Ben Tre
spots.note: Young coconut on the river path. Come for the water in front of you, then walk.

sections.heading: Fine dining and other kitchens
paragraphs: Book the three rooms below. They are dinners, not walk-in noodle shops. Hours change, so confirm the day.
Korean barbecue and Japanese counters cluster in the lanes inland of My Khe, around An Thuong. Walk until a room is busy. This page does not pick one shop there.

spots.name: Nen
spots.address: 16 Mỹ Đà Tây 2, Ngũ Hành Sơn
spots.note: A contemporary Vietnamese tasting menu, and a Michelin Green Star kitchen. Book. Lunch is not served every day. Dinner is the sitting to count on.

spots.name: Le Comptoir
spots.address: 16 Chế Lan Viên, Ngũ Hành Sơn
spots.note: French bistro cooking, with a short menu and a wine list. Dinner, booked. The two Ngũ Hành Sơn rooms are a ride from the river, so go for the meal.

spots.name: The Temptation
spots.note: French, toward the Son Tra shore on Hồ Nghinh. Dinner is the reliable service. Monday is dinner only. Confirm the lunch hour on other days.

sections.heading: After dark
paragraphs: The beach road is the night. Cocktails sit a lane inland, where the address is a side street and not the sand. Go after dinner. These rooms are drinks, with food if you are already there.

spots.name: East West Brewing
spots.address: My Khe beachfront. Street: check on arrival.
spots.note: House beer with the sea in front of you. The taproom page says beachfront and 08:00–01:00, and it does not print a street. Confirm the door.

spots.name: Esco Beach
spots.note: A beachfront room for a meal and a late drink, with the sand as the view. It runs long. Confirm the night’s music when you arrive.

spots.name: Kala Kala
spots.note: A beach club: pool, music, and a late close. Go for the afternoon into the night. It is the wrong room for a quiet noodle.

spots.name: Firebirds Tropical
spots.note: Cocktails in a garden lane, one turn inland from the beach road. It is easy to walk past. Ask the bartender if you want a drink off the printed list.

spots.name: Firebirds Vietnamese Craft
spots.address: City center. Confirm the street on arrival.
spots.note: The second Firebirds room, newer, and dressed with Vietnamese furniture. The street is not fixed on this page. Confirm it before you go.

sections.heading: A ride away
paragraphs: Hoi An is under an hour by the coast road. Go there for cao lau, white rose dumplings, and the old-town dinner you will not get on My Khe.

Hue is the other direction, over Hai Van or by the tunnel. Bun bo Hue belongs to that city. Eat it there if the bowl is the reason for the trip. The Da Nang shops for both noodles are in the noodle list above, for the day you stay in town.

seoTitle: Da Nang food guide — noodles, seafood, cafes, bars
seoDescription: What to eat in Da Nang: mi Quang at lunch, Huynh Thuc Khang at breakfast, and seafood on Vo Nguyen Giap. Market clocks disagree, so check the door.
